title: Robots & Physical Automation Displacement by 2030
description: Projected percentage of physical/manual task jobs displaced by industrial robots, warehouse automation, and other physical AI systems by 2030. Synthesizes IFR installation data, academic studies on robot-worker substitution, and institutional forecasts on automation of predictable physical tasks.

sources.title: Robots and Jobs: Evidence from US Labor Markets
sources.excerpt: One more robot per thousand workers reduces the employment-to-population ratio by 0.2 percentage points and wages by 0.42%. Between 1990 and 2007, the increase in robots reduced employment by about 400,000 workers.

sources.title: The Simple Macroeconomics of AI
sources.excerpt: Automation always produces a positive productivity effect on wages by reducing costs; simultaneously, it displaces workers from the tasks they used to perform. Net displacement from all AI and automation estimated at 1-5% of employment.

sources.title: World Robotics 2025 — Industrial Robots
sources.excerpt: 542,000 industrial robots installed in 2024 — more than double the number 10 years ago. 4,664,000 robots operational worldwide. US installations at 34,200 units. Global market value $16.5 billion.

sources.title: Future of Jobs Report 2025
sources.excerpt: Robotics and automation expected to drive business transformation for 58% of employers. Robots and automation forecast to displace 5 million more jobs than they create. 92 million jobs displaced, 170 million created, net +78 million by 2030.

sources.title: Agents, Robots, and Us: Skill Partnerships in the Age of AI
sources.excerpt: 57% of US work hours are technically automatable. Physical tasks comprise 50%+ of hours for 40% of the US workforce. Robot unit costs ($150-500K) must fall to $20-50K for mass physical automation adoption. At least 14% of employees globally may need career changes by 2030.

sources.title: The Risk of Automation for Jobs in OECD Countries
sources.excerpt: 14% of jobs across OECD countries are at high risk of automation. An additional 32% may be significantly changed but not eliminated. 27% of jobs at high risk when including all automation technologies including AI.

sources.title: Industry and Occupational Employment Projections Overview 2024-34
sources.excerpt: Retail trade projected to decline 1.2% as automation and e-commerce reduce sales occupations. Mining/extraction declining 1.6% driven by robotics and drones. Total employment projected to grow 3.1% (2024-34), much slower than prior decade.

sources.title: Amazon Fulfillment Center Robotics Deployment
sources.excerpt: Amazon deployed roughly 800,000 mobile robots across its fulfillment centers by 2024, making it the largest private deployer of mobile robots globally.

sources.title: The Dawn of Humanoid Robots and Physical AI
sources.excerpt: Physically demanding or outdoor work unlikely to be affected by current AI. Projects 50,000-100,000 humanoid robot shipments in 2026. Unit economics expected to reach $15,000-$20,000 per robot.

sources.title: Jobs at High Risk of Automation in the US
sources.excerpt: 15% of US jobs — about 23 million total — are at high risk of displacement due to automation, concentrated in manufacturing, transportation, and food preparation.

sources.title: US Manufacturing Employment Declines as Automation Ramps Up
sources.excerpt: US manufacturing lost 78,000 jobs over the past year with 12,000 cuts in August alone. Manufacturing employment at lowest level since onset of COVID-19 pandemic.

sources.title: How Robots Affect Employment
sources.publisher: Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis
sources.excerpt: Robots have a mixed effect: replacing jobs that relatively high-wage manufacturing employees used to perform, while also making firms more efficient and productive. One robot per thousand workers replaced about six workers.

sources.title: Top 5 Global Robotics Trends 2026
sources.excerpt: The global market value of industrial robot installations has reached an all-time high of US$16.7 billion. IFR names five 2026 trends: (1) AI and Autonomy in Robotics, (2) Robots gain versatility as IT meets OT, (3) Humanoids to prove reliability and efficiency, (4) Safety and Security, (5) Robots as allies in tackling labor gaps. Humanoid robots need to match high industrial requirements towards cycle times, energy consumption and maintenance costs. Employers around the world are struggling to find people with the specialized skills required.

sources.title: Amazon's Automation Push: 1 Million Robots and Plans to Avoid Hiring 600,000 Workers
sources.excerpt: Amazon crossed 1 million robots deployed globally by mid-2025. Internal documents reviewed by The New York Times show Amazon's robotics team has an 'ultimate goal to automate 75 percent of the company's operations.' Executives told Amazon's board that robotic automation could prevent the need to hire more than 600,000 new workers as sales are expected to double by 2033. By 2027, Amazon's automation team expects to avoid hiring over 160,000 U.S. workers it would normally need, saving 'about 30 cents on every item it packs and delivers.'

sources.title: Amazon unveils latest warehouse robot as tech giants continue AI layoffs
sources.excerpt: Amazon unveiled next-generation Proteus, an autonomous mobile robot that takes commands in conversational language, at its 'Delivering the Future' event in London. The original Proteus, deployed since 2022, is now in 25 U.S. fulfillment centers, with the new version rolling out in Europe in H1 2027. Amazon has eliminated 30,000 corporate positions since October as it prioritizes AI initiatives. Amazon UK/Ireland VP John Boumphrey told CNBC: 'our experience of robots is that it's driven up employment rather than the reverse.'

sources.title: UPS's Robot Army Just Cut Package Costs by 28%
sources.excerpt: UPS has automated 127 facilities to date. Package volume through automated facilities was 57% in 2023, projected to reach 68% by end of 2026. 24 additional facilities are slated for automation in 2026. CEO Carol Tomé stated 'the cost per piece in automated buildings is 28% lower than in conventional, non-automated buildings.' UPS uses pick-and-place systems for small package sorting, Pickle Robots to unload trucks, and autonomous guided vehicles.

sources.title: Immiserizing Automation
sources.publisher: CREi / Barcelona School of Economics (Asriyan, Reichardt, Shelegia)
sources.excerpt: Calibrating an overlapping-generations model with career ladders to the 1980 US economy: "Acemoglu and Restrepo (2020) estimate that cost savings from robots were around 30%. At that level, Figure 5 implies a positive output effect of about 2.6%... the same technical change would have raised output by roughly 3.5%... Wage backloading thus dissipates around a quarter of the potential gain." On participation: "with 30% cost savings, the model predicts a 4.5 percentage-point fall in the participation rate," against an observed rise in the share of 20-to-59-year-old men out of the labor force from 10.4% in 1980 to 15.0% in 2019. Cost savings and participation, not share of physical tasks automated, so this is recorded as an overlay rather than a plotted point.

sources.title: A Turbulent AI Era and Critical Choices to Make
sources.excerpt: "I think 'smart' robots will begin to compete with people on some physical tasks - in the construction and hospitality industries, for example - by the end of the decade." Gates adds that "Many Americans I talk to don't realize how fast dexterous robots are advancing because much of the advanced work is being done in other countries, primarily China," and that once one firm adopts and cuts prices, "its competitors will feel immense pressure to do the same." Commentary essay; no original data.
